steps.action: Call your bank now, or dial 159. Say you were tricked into buying or sending crypto, and ask them to block any more payments and try to get your money back.
steps.contact: 159, or the number on the back of your card

steps.action: Report the scam to Report Fraud, the police's national fraud line. If you live in Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101 instead.
steps.organisation: Report Fraud (police national fraud reporting centre)

steps.action: If your bank will not help, complain to the bank first. If you are still unhappy, contact the Financial Ombudsman Service within 6 months of the bank's final letter. It can look at what your bank did, but usually not at the crypto company.
Also tell the Financial Conduct Authority about the scam. Be careful: anyone who calls offering to recover your crypto for a fee is likely another scammer.

extra.notes: No reimbursement scheme covers crypto itself; the FCA says most crypto activity is unregulated, with no Ombudsman or FSCS cover for the crypto firm. The Ombudsman can still review the bank that sent the money (including 'me-to-me' transfers to your own crypto account). No official page found naming an exchange freeze step, so none is listed.
